about.title: Rio Vista Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Vista is a small town of about 8,348 people, and when someone dies here because of another person's carelessness, the absence is felt on Main Street, along River Road and out on Route 12. Solano County's most recent final collision year, 2025, recorded no traffic deaths within the city, and that is worth acknowledging plainly. Even so, wrongful death claims are not limited to crashes. They also grow out of unsafe premises, defective products, medical errors and workplace incidents. California law gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a civil claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when no closer relative exists. Most families have two years from the date of death to act; if a public agency may be responsible, that window narrows considerably. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive simply connects you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these matters on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Rio Vista Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're connected with can sort out quickly whether you are eligible and how multiple relatives are handled.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: The general two-year deadline runs from the date of death, and it is shorter when a city, county, state or other government body is involved. Learning where you stand early keeps a Rio Vista family from losing rights simply because time passed.

items.title: A Civil Path Separate From Any Criminal Case
items.desc: A wrongful death action is your family's own claim for funeral costs, lost support and lost companionship, regardless of whether prosecutors file charges. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on Route 12 just outside Rio Vista. Does the location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Route 12 is a state highway, so if road design, signage or maintenance is part of the picture, a public entity may be involved and the filing deadline becomes much shorter than the standard two years. An independent attorney can review the collision report and identify every party early, before any deadline becomes a problem.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action that your family controls, and it can move forward while a criminal case is pending. The outcomes are independent of one another, though evidence from the criminal matter can sometimes be useful. Waiting is not required, and the two-year clock keeps running regardless.

items.question: Our loved one was retired and not earning income. Is a claim still possible?
items.answer: Yes. California wrongful death law recognizes losses beyond a paycheck, including funeral and burial costs and the loss of love, companionship, comfort and guidance the person provided. Household contributions and support to dependents also count. An attorney can explain how these losses are documented in a specific case.
